frozen_candidate_root_contribution: د-ن-و marks occupying or moving toward the PROXIMAL/LOW pole of a salient scale relative to a reference point. The default axis is spatial (near, close, within reach, low / hanging-low), and the single relational primitive extends productively along whatever axis context supplies: temporal immediacy (al-dunyā = the near/present life vs the latter al-ākhira), lesser quantity (adnā vs akthar), lesser magnitude (al-ʿadhāb al-adnā vs al-akbar), inferior rank/value (adnā vs khayr), and proximity-to-an-outcome (adnā an … = 'more conducive'). The root supplies only the near/low RELATION; the 'world / life / fruit / sky' content and any moral negativity come from the modified head noun and the ākhira contrast, never from the root itself.

The default axis is spatial (near, close, within reach, low / hanging-low), and the single relational primitive extends productively along whatever axis context supplies: temporal immediacy (al-dunyā = the near/present life vs the latter al-ākhira), lesser quantity (adnā vs akthar), lesser magnitude (al-ʿadhāb al-adnā vs al-akbar), inferior rank/value (adnā vs khayr), and proximity-to-an-outcome (adnā an … = 'more conducive'). internal_discovery.plain_explanation: Every form of this root places something at the 'near' or 'low' end of some scale, measured from a reference point. Concretely it is physical nearness: a person who 'drew near' (danā, 53:8), garments 'drawn down/close' (yudnīna, 33:59), fruit and shade 'within reach / low-hanging' (dāniyah). The comparative adnā is 'nearer / lower / lesser' on whatever scale is in view — distance, amount, size, worth, or nearness-to-a-result. The dominant word al-dunyā is just the feminine of that comparative, 'the nearer/lower one', frozen for 'this present life' set against al-ākhira 'the latter life' — and the corpus keeps the literal sense visible by using al-dunyā for 'the nearest heaven' (67:5). So this is one relational idea ('near/low on a scale'), not several unrelated meanings.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: د-ن-و does NOT denote 'world / earth / cosmos / life' as substance (those come from the elided head ḥayāt/dār/samāʾ, and are falsified as root content by «ٱلسَّمَآءَ ٱلدُّنْيَا» = nearest sky and «أَدْنَى ٱلْأَرْضِ» = nearer land); NOT motion in itself (adnā and dānin are static; only danā/yudnī add movement); NOT contact / arrival / union ('or nearer' at 53:9 measures a residual gap; dāniyah fruit is within reach, not touching); NOT intrinsic moral vileness or blameworthiness (nearness is a REWARD for Paradise's fruit and shade at 55:54/69:23/76:14; the negativity clinging to al-dunyā is supplied by the ākhira contrast, not the root); NOT affective intimacy/kinship (the nearness is positional-scalar, never relational-affective); NOT a bare tense/'present-first' notion (the temporal reading of dunyā is parasitic on near/far plus the ākhira antonym).
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: 2:61:27:1 «أَتَسْتَبْدِلُونَ ٱلَّذِى هُوَ أَدْنَىٰ بِٱلَّذِى هُوَ خَيْرٌ»: the two exchanged items are foods, so nothing is spatially, temporally or numerically nearer; only the rank/value reading (adnā = baser/inferior, opposed to khayr) works. This is the point where the spatial-nearness nucleus is furthest from the surface, absorbed only by the low->inferior extension — which the Quran attests independently at 7:169 («عَرَضَ هَٰذَا ٱلْأَدْنَىٰ» opposed to «ٱلدَّارُ ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ») but never explicitly derives.
internal_discovery.strongest_competitor: A two-nucleus SPLIT: (A) neutral spatial PROXIMITY (verbs danā/yudnī, participles dānin/dāniyah, adnā-of-distance, and al-samāʾ al-dunyā) versus (B) evaluative LOWNESS / a synchronically frozen noun al-dunyā = 'this deprecated transient world' with no live 'nearness' content — motivated by dunyā's 86% dominance, its conventionalization, and the apparent contradiction that 'nearness' is a positive feature of the hereafter (dāniyah fruit) yet al-dunyā names the depreciated order. It LOSES Quran-internally: the split has no morphological or distributional seam (A and B share the identical afʿal/fuʿlā elative), and the corpus itself dissolves it — 67:5 uses the very word al-dunyā for 'the nearest heaven' (class-A spatial), and 7:169 uses the masculine elative hādhā al-adnā in al-dunyā's exact slot ('the goods of this lower [world]', opposed to al-dār al-ākhira khayr), welding the evaluative-'lower', the 'this-world', and the elative senses into a single word and a single verse. A two-nucleus theory would have to cut through single words and single verses.

It LOSES Quran-internally: the split has no morphological or distributional seam (A and B share the identical afʿal/fuʿlā elative), and the corpus itself dissolves it — 67:5 uses the very word al-dunyā for 'the nearest heaven' (class-A spatial), and 7:169 uses the masculine elative hādhā al-adnā in al-dunyā's exact slot ('the goods of this lower [world]', opposed to al-dār al-ākhira khayr), welding the evaluative-'lower', the 'this-world', and the elative senses into a single word and a single verse. internal_discovery.rationale: All three lenses converge (no split survives) on one narrow relational nucleus: 'the near/low pole of a scale.' The nucleus is anchored by hard spatial data that admit no world/life reading — danā 53:8 ('drew near'), the four participles of physical reach, adnā al-arḍ 30:3, qāba qawsayni aw adnā 53:9 — and is welded across classes by three demonstrated corpus-internal bridges: 53:8↔53:9 (verb danā and elative aw adnā in adjacent āyāt on one distance scale), 67:5 (al-dunyā = nearest heaven, still transparently spatial), and 7:169 (masculine al-adnā occupying al-dunyā's slot, opposed to al-ākhira). The quantitative (58:7, 73:20) and magnitude (32:21) elatives fill the scale without strain. Two edges are honestly softer — 2:61 (adnā = inferior, only the value axis works) and the «adnā an …» epistemic set (proximity-to-outcome) — but both are corpus-consistent extensions of the same pole rather than counterexamples requiring a second nucleus; they are flagged as adversarial boundaries. The dominant al-dunyā is a lexicalized application of the elative, not an independent sense, so the judgment is genuinely ROOT-WIDE with STRONG support and no unbridged class.

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: Finite verbs of literal proximity: intransitive danā 'drew near / approached' (53:8, paired with fa-tadallā 'then hung down/descended') and the form-IV causative yudnīna 'draw/bring [garments] near/down over' (33:59). The clearest, most literal exponent of the near/low nucleus, with and without transitivity.
clusters.classification_rationale: Both tokens are qac_pos=V and are the only finite verbs; surface danaA (intransitive perfect) vs yudoniy (causative imperfect). Pure spatial approach / bringing-near, no world/life or evaluative content.
clusters.supporting_evidence_note: 53:8:2:1 «ثُمَّ دَنَا فَتَدَلَّىٰ»; 33:59:8:1 «يُدْنِينَ عَلَيْهِنَّ مِن جَلَٰبِيبِهِنَّ». 53:8 sits one āya before the elative «أَوْ أَدْنَىٰ» (53:9) on the same distance scale, welding the verb layer to the elative layer.

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: Active participle dānin/dāniyah 'near / within reach / low-hanging' — a stative spatial proximity with the nuance 'close enough to reach.' Three of four describe Paradise's fruit/shade as an accessible blessing, one is ordinary agriculture.
clusters.classification_rationale: Surface daAn-/daAniyap- participial forms (qac_pos N or ADJ), isolated by explicit word_refs. State of nearness with no motion and no negative charge.
clusters.supporting_evidence_note: 6:99:24:1 «قِنْوَانٌ دَانِيَةٌ» (agriculture); 55:54:9:1 «وَجَنَى ٱلْجَنَّتَيْنِ دَانٍ»; 69:23:2:1 «قُطُوفُهَا دَانِيَةٌ»; 76:14:1:2 «وَدَانِيَةً عَلَيْهِمْ ظِلَٰلُهَا». Nearness applied to a reward proves the root is not intrinsically pejorative.

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: Elative adnā 'nearer / lower / lesser', one morphological form whose scale is supplied by context: spatial (30:3 adnā al-arḍ; 53:9 aw adnā), quantity vs akthar (58:7; 73:20 adnā min thulthay al-layl, the lone T token), magnitude vs al-akbar (32:21 al-ʿadhāb al-adnā), rank/value vs khayr (2:61; 7:169 ʿaraḍa hādhā al-adnā), and proximity-to-outcome (the «adnā an …» set = 'more conducive'). All reduce to 'the near/low end of a scale.'
clusters.classification_rationale: All twelve >adonaY tokens (qac_pos N/ADJ/T), isolated by explicit word_refs. The single shifting antonym (akthar, al-akbar, khayr, and — via dunyā — al-ākhira) confirms 'proximal/low pole of A scale', not any one fixed dimension. 7:169 is the masculine elative standing in al-dunyā's slot, the decisive bridge to the dominant form.
clusters.supporting_evidence_note: Spatial/quantitative core (30:3, 53:9, 58:7, 73:20, 32:21) is neutral and hard-anchored. TWO softer edges are flagged as adversarial boundaries, not counterexamples: 2:61:27:1 «أَتَسْتَبْدِلُونَ ٱلَّذِى هُوَ أَدْنَىٰ بِٱلَّذِى هُوَ خَيْرٌ»: the two exchanged items are foods, so nothing is spatially, temporally or numerically nearer; only the rank/value reading (adnā = baser/inferior, opposed to khayr) works. This is the point where the spatial-nearness nucleus is furthest from the surface, absorbed only by the low->inferior extension — which the Quran attests independently at 7:169 («عَرَضَ هَٰذَا ٱلْأَدْنَىٰ» opposed to «ٱلدَّارُ ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ») but never explicitly derives. ALSO: The «أَدْنَىٰٓ أَن …» set (2:282, 4:3, 5:108, 33:51, 33:59:13:1) reads adnā as 'nearer to bringing about outcome X' = 'more conducive/apt', projecting proximity onto an abstract goal; this is consistent with the near/low-pole nucleus (proximity to a target is still proximity) but the Quran nowhere glosses the metaphor, so the proximity-to-outcome step is a reasoned extension, not a surface-demonstrated identity.

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: al-dunyā, the lexicalized feminine elative 'the nearer/lower one', frozen for 'this present life / world' and almost always yoked to al-ākhira 'the latter/further'. A lexicalized sub-node of the elative, NOT an independent 'world' sense: the root still contributes only 'the nearer one', with 'life/world' from the (often elided) head ḥayāt and the negativity from the ākhira contrast.

reconciliation.rationale: Absorbed as the value-axis of the one pole (low->inferior), independently attested by 7:169 (hādhā al-adnā opposed to al-ākhira khayr). Retained as an ADVERSARIAL_BOUNDARY because the metaphor is attested but never explicitly derived.

Absorbed as proximity-to-outcome ('nearer to bringing X about'); reinforced by 33:59 which contains BOTH the concrete yudnīna and the abstract adnā an in one verse. Flagged as an adversarial boundary since the surface does not state the scale.

adversarial_verification.notes: A genuine refutation was run: the strongest competitor — a two-nucleus split of neutral spatial PROXIMITY (verbs, participles, adnā-of-distance, al-samāʾ al-dunyā) versus evaluative LOWNESS / a frozen al-dunyā = 'world' — was tested against the corpus and returned SUPPORTED for unity, i.e. the split failed. It is dissolved by single-word/single-verse counter-evidence: 67:5 uses al-dunyā spatially ('nearest heaven') and 7:169 puts 'this-world', 'lower-in-value', and the elative into one word (hādhā al-adnā), so a split would have to cut through single words. The claim is falsifiable (a substance-'world' or affect token would break it) and distinctive from the nearness neighbour ق-ر-ب by specifically covering the LOW/LESSER pole (quantity, magnitude, rank) and the lexicalized dunyā. The two soft edges (2:61, adnā-an) are consistent extensions, not failing occurrences requiring a second nucleus.

occurrence_dispositions.note: All twelve >adonaY tokens (qac_pos N/ADJ/T), isolated by explicit word_refs. The single shifting antonym (akthar, al-akbar, khayr, and — via dunyā — al-ākhira) confirms 'proximal/low pole of A scale', not any one fixed dimension. 7:169 is the masculine elative standing in al-dunyā's slot, the decisive bridge to the dominant form.
occurrence_dispositions.candidate_semantic_interpretation: Elative adnā 'nearer / lower / lesser', one morphological form whose scale is supplied by context: spatial (30:3 adnā al-arḍ; 53:9 aw adnā), quantity vs akthar (58:7; 73:20 adnā min thulthay al-layl, the lone T token), magnitude vs al-akbar (32:21 al-ʿadhāb al-adnā), rank/value vs khayr (2:61; 7:169 ʿaraḍa hādhā al-adnā), and proximity-to-outcome (the «adnā an …» set = 'more conducive'). All reduce to 'the near/low end of a scale.'
occurrence_dispositions.cluster_supporting_evidence: Spatial/quantitative core (30:3, 53:9, 58:7, 73:20, 32:21) is neutral and hard-anchored. TWO softer edges are flagged as adversarial boundaries, not counterexamples: 2:61:27:1 «أَتَسْتَبْدِلُونَ ٱلَّذِى هُوَ أَدْنَىٰ بِٱلَّذِى هُوَ خَيْرٌ»: the two exchanged items are foods, so nothing is spatially, temporally or numerically nearer; only the rank/value reading (adnā = baser/inferior, opposed to khayr) works. This is the point where the spatial-nearness nucleus is furthest from the surface, absorbed only by the low->inferior extension — which the Quran attests independently at 7:169 («عَرَضَ هَٰذَا ٱلْأَدْنَىٰ» opposed to «ٱلدَّارُ ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ») but never explicitly derives. ALSO: The «أَدْنَىٰٓ أَن …» set (2:282, 4:3, 5:108, 33:51, 33:59:13:1) reads adnā as 'nearer to bringing about outcome X' = 'more conducive/apt', projecting proximity onto an abstract goal; this is consistent with the near/low-pole nucleus (proximity to a target is still proximity) but the Quran nowhere glosses the metaphor, so the proximity-to-outcome step is a reasoned extension, not a surface-demonstrated identity.

occurrence_dispositions.note: All twelve >adonaY tokens (qac_pos N/ADJ/T), isolated by explicit word_refs. The single shifting antonym (akthar, al-akbar, khayr, and — via dunyā — al-ākhira) confirms 'proximal/low pole of A scale', not any one fixed dimension. 7:169 is the masculine elative standing in al-dunyā's slot, the decisive bridge to the dominant form.
occurrence_dispositions.candidate_semantic_interpretation: Elative adnā 'nearer / lower / lesser', one morphological form whose scale is supplied by context: spatial (30:3 adnā al-arḍ; 53:9 aw adnā), quantity vs akthar (58:7; 73:20 adnā min thulthay al-layl, the lone T token), magnitude vs al-akbar (32:21 al-ʿadhāb al-adnā), rank/value vs khayr (2:61; 7:169 ʿaraḍa hādhā al-adnā), and proximity-to-outcome (the «adnā an …» set = 'more conducive'). All reduce to 'the near/low end of a scale.'
occurrence_dispositions.cluster_supporting_evidence: Spatial/quantitative core (30:3, 53:9, 58:7, 73:20, 32:21) is neutral and hard-anchored. TWO softer edges are flagged as adversarial boundaries, not counterexamples: 2:61:27:1 «أَتَسْتَبْدِلُونَ ٱلَّذِى هُوَ أَدْنَىٰ بِٱلَّذِى هُوَ خَيْرٌ»: the two exchanged items are foods, so nothing is spatially, temporally or numerically nearer; only the rank/value reading (adnā = baser/inferior, opposed to khayr) works. This is the point where the spatial-nearness nucleus is furthest from the surface, absorbed only by the low->inferior extension — which the Quran attests independently at 7:169 («عَرَضَ هَٰذَا ٱلْأَدْنَىٰ» opposed to «ٱلدَّارُ ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ») but never explicitly derives. ALSO: The «أَدْنَىٰٓ أَن …» set (2:282, 4:3, 5:108, 33:51, 33:59:13:1) reads adnā as 'nearer to bringing about outcome X' = 'more conducive/apt', projecting proximity onto an abstract goal; this is consistent with the near/low-pole nucleus (proximity to a target is still proximity) but the Quran nowhere glosses the metaphor, so the proximity-to-outcome step is a reasoned extension, not a surface-demonstrated identity.

The single shifting antonym (akthar, al-akbar, khayr, and — via dunyā — al-ākhira) confirms 'proximal/low pole of A scale', not any one fixed dimension. 7:169 is the masculine elative standing in al-dunyā's slot, the decisive bridge to the dominant form.
occurrence_dispositions.candidate_semantic_interpretation: Elative adnā 'nearer / lower / lesser', one morphological form whose scale is supplied by context: spatial (30:3 adnā al-arḍ; 53:9 aw adnā), quantity vs akthar (58:7; 73:20 adnā min thulthay al-layl, the lone T token), magnitude vs al-akbar (32:21 al-ʿadhāb al-adnā), rank/value vs khayr (2:61; 7:169 ʿaraḍa hādhā al-adnā), and proximity-to-outcome (the «adnā an …» set = 'more conducive'). All reduce to 'the near/low end of a scale.'
occurrence_dispositions.cluster_supporting_evidence: Spatial/quantitative core (30:3, 53:9, 58:7, 73:20, 32:21) is neutral and hard-anchored. TWO softer edges are flagged as adversarial boundaries, not counterexamples: 2:61:27:1 «أَتَسْتَبْدِلُونَ ٱلَّذِى هُوَ أَدْنَىٰ بِٱلَّذِى هُوَ خَيْرٌ»: the two exchanged items are foods, so nothing is spatially, temporally or numerically nearer; only the rank/value reading (adnā = baser/inferior, opposed to khayr) works. This is the point where the spatial-nearness nucleus is furthest from the surface, absorbed only by the low->inferior extension — which the Quran attests independently at 7:169 («عَرَضَ هَٰذَا ٱلْأَدْنَىٰ» opposed to «ٱلدَّارُ ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ») but never explicitly derives. ALSO: The «أَدْنَىٰٓ أَن …» set (2:282, 4:3, 5:108, 33:51, 33:59:13:1) reads adnā as 'nearer to bringing about outcome X' = 'more conducive/apt', projecting proximity onto an abstract goal; this is consistent with the near/low-pole nucleus (proximity to a target is still proximity) but the Quran nowhere glosses the metaphor, so the proximity-to-outcome step is a reasoned extension, not a surface-demonstrated identity.

occurrence_dispositions.candidate_semantic_interpretation: Elative adnā 'nearer / lower / lesser', one morphological form whose scale is supplied by context: spatial (30:3 adnā al-arḍ; 53:9 aw adnā), quantity vs akthar (58:7; 73:20 adnā min thulthay al-layl, the lone T token), magnitude vs al-akbar (32:21 al-ʿadhāb al-adnā), rank/value vs khayr (2:61; 7:169 ʿaraḍa hādhā al-adnā), and proximity-to-outcome (the «adnā an …» set = 'more conducive'). All reduce to 'the near/low end of a scale.'
occurrence_dispositions.cluster_supporting_evidence: Spatial/quantitative core (30:3, 53:9, 58:7, 73:20, 32:21) is neutral and hard-anchored. TWO softer edges are flagged as adversarial boundaries, not counterexamples: 2:61:27:1 «أَتَسْتَبْدِلُونَ ٱلَّذِى هُوَ أَدْنَىٰ بِٱلَّذِى هُوَ خَيْرٌ»: the two exchanged items are foods, so nothing is spatially, temporally or numerically nearer; only the rank/value reading (adnā = baser/inferior, opposed to khayr) works. This is the point where the spatial-nearness nucleus is furthest from the surface, absorbed only by the low->inferior extension — which the Quran attests independently at 7:169 («عَرَضَ هَٰذَا ٱلْأَدْنَىٰ» opposed to «ٱلدَّارُ ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ») but never explicitly derives. ALSO: The «أَدْنَىٰٓ أَن …» set (2:282, 4:3, 5:108, 33:51, 33:59:13:1) reads adnā as 'nearer to bringing about outcome X' = 'more conducive/apt', projecting proximity onto an abstract goal; this is consistent with the near/low-pole nucleus (proximity to a target is still proximity) but the Quran nowhere glosses the metaphor, so the proximity-to-outcome step is a reasoned extension, not a surface-demonstrated identity.

occurrence_dispositions.note: «قَابَ قَوْسَيْنِ أَوْ أَدْنَىٰ» sits one āya after danā (53:8); 'or nearer' measures a residual distance, welding verb and elative on one spatial scale and confirming near != contact.
occurrence_dispositions.candidate_semantic_interpretation: Elative adnā 'nearer / lower / lesser', one morphological form whose scale is supplied by context: spatial (30:3 adnā al-arḍ; 53:9 aw adnā), quantity vs akthar (58:7; 73:20 adnā min thulthay al-layl, the lone T token), magnitude vs al-akbar (32:21 al-ʿadhāb al-adnā), rank/value vs khayr (2:61; 7:169 ʿaraḍa hādhā al-adnā), and proximity-to-outcome (the «adnā an …» set = 'more conducive'). All reduce to 'the near/low end of a scale.'
occurrence_dispositions.cluster_supporting_evidence: Spatial/quantitative core (30:3, 53:9, 58:7, 73:20, 32:21) is neutral and hard-anchored. TWO softer edges are flagged as adversarial boundaries, not counterexamples: 2:61:27:1 «أَتَسْتَبْدِلُونَ ٱلَّذِى هُوَ أَدْنَىٰ بِٱلَّذِى هُوَ خَيْرٌ»: the two exchanged items are foods, so nothing is spatially, temporally or numerically nearer; only the rank/value reading (adnā = baser/inferior, opposed to khayr) works. This is the point where the spatial-nearness nucleus is furthest from the surface, absorbed only by the low->inferior extension — which the Quran attests independently at 7:169 («عَرَضَ هَٰذَا ٱلْأَدْنَىٰ» opposed to «ٱلدَّارُ ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ») but never explicitly derives. ALSO: The «أَدْنَىٰٓ أَن …» set (2:282, 4:3, 5:108, 33:51, 33:59:13:1) reads adnā as 'nearer to bringing about outcome X' = 'more conducive/apt', projecting proximity onto an abstract goal; this is consistent with the near/low-pole nucleus (proximity to a target is still proximity) but the Quran nowhere glosses the metaphor, so the proximity-to-outcome step is a reasoned extension, not a surface-demonstrated identity.
occurrence_dispositions.preliminary_note: All twelve >adonaY tokens (qac_pos N/ADJ/T), isolated by explicit word_refs. The single shifting antonym (akthar, al-akbar, khayr, and — via dunyā — al-ākhira) confirms 'proximal/low pole of A scale', not any one fixed dimension. 7:169 is the masculine elative standing in al-dunyā's slot, the decisive bridge to the dominant form.

occurrence_dispositions.note: All twelve >adonaY tokens (qac_pos N/ADJ/T), isolated by explicit word_refs. The single shifting antonym (akthar, al-akbar, khayr, and — via dunyā — al-ākhira) confirms 'proximal/low pole of A scale', not any one fixed dimension. 7:169 is the masculine elative standing in al-dunyā's slot, the decisive bridge to the dominant form.
occurrence_dispositions.candidate_semantic_interpretation: Elative adnā 'nearer / lower / lesser', one morphological form whose scale is supplied by context: spatial (30:3 adnā al-arḍ; 53:9 aw adnā), quantity vs akthar (58:7; 73:20 adnā min thulthay al-layl, the lone T token), magnitude vs al-akbar (32:21 al-ʿadhāb al-adnā), rank/value vs khayr (2:61; 7:169 ʿaraḍa hādhā al-adnā), and proximity-to-outcome (the «adnā an …» set = 'more conducive'). All reduce to 'the near/low end of a scale.'
occurrence_dispositions.cluster_supporting_evidence: Spatial/quantitative core (30:3, 53:9, 58:7, 73:20, 32:21) is neutral and hard-anchored. TWO softer edges are flagged as adversarial boundaries, not counterexamples: 2:61:27:1 «أَتَسْتَبْدِلُونَ ٱلَّذِى هُوَ أَدْنَىٰ بِٱلَّذِى هُوَ خَيْرٌ»: the two exchanged items are foods, so nothing is spatially, temporally or numerically nearer; only the rank/value reading (adnā = baser/inferior, opposed to khayr) works. This is the point where the spatial-nearness nucleus is furthest from the surface, absorbed only by the low->inferior extension — which the Quran attests independently at 7:169 («عَرَضَ هَٰذَا ٱلْأَدْنَىٰ» opposed to «ٱلدَّارُ ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ») but never explicitly derives. ALSO: The «أَدْنَىٰٓ أَن …» set (2:282, 4:3, 5:108, 33:51, 33:59:13:1) reads adnā as 'nearer to bringing about outcome X' = 'more conducive/apt', projecting proximity onto an abstract goal; this is consistent with the near/low-pole nucleus (proximity to a target is still proximity) but the Quran nowhere glosses the metaphor, so the proximity-to-outcome step is a reasoned extension, not a surface-demonstrated identity.

occurrence_dispositions.candidate_semantic_interpretation: Elative adnā 'nearer / lower / lesser', one morphological form whose scale is supplied by context: spatial (30:3 adnā al-arḍ; 53:9 aw adnā), quantity vs akthar (58:7; 73:20 adnā min thulthay al-layl, the lone T token), magnitude vs al-akbar (32:21 al-ʿadhāb al-adnā), rank/value vs khayr (2:61; 7:169 ʿaraḍa hādhā al-adnā), and proximity-to-outcome (the «adnā an …» set = 'more conducive'). This is the point where the spatial-nearness nucleus is furthest from the surface, absorbed only by the low->inferior extension — which the Quran attests independently at 7:169 («عَرَضَ هَٰذَا ٱلْأَدْنَىٰ» opposed to «ٱلدَّارُ ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ») but never explicitly derives. ALSO: The «أَدْنَىٰٓ أَن …» set (2:282, 4:3, 5:108, 33:51, 33:59:13:1) reads adnā as 'nearer to bringing about outcome X' = 'more conducive/apt', projecting proximity onto an abstract goal; this is consistent with the near/low-pole nucleus (proximity to a target is still proximity) but the Quran nowhere glosses the metaphor, so the proximity-to-outcome step is a reasoned extension, not a surface-demonstrated identity.
occurrence_dispositions.preliminary_note: All twelve >adonaY tokens (qac_pos N/ADJ/T), isolated by explicit word_refs. The single shifting antonym (akthar, al-akbar, khayr, and — via dunyā — al-ākhira) confirms 'proximal/low pole of A scale', not any one fixed dimension. 7:169 is the masculine elative standing in al-dunyā's slot, the decisive bridge to the dominant form.

independent_verification: Three independent lenses (A account, B account, C adversarial) converged on the single near/low-pole nucleus; the adversary's own split attempt collapsed on 67:5 and 7:169.
candidate_root_contribution: د-ن-و marks occupying or moving toward the PROXIMAL/LOW pole of a salient scale relative to a reference point. The default axis is spatial (near, close, within reach, low / hanging-low), and the single relational primitive extends productively along whatever axis context supplies: temporal immediacy (al-dunyā = the near/present life vs the latter al-ākhira), lesser quantity (adnā vs akthar), lesser magnitude (al-ʿadhāb al-adnā vs al-akbar), inferior rank/value (adnā vs khayr), and proximity-to-an-outcome (adnā an … = 'more conducive'). The root supplies only the near/low RELATION; the 'world / life / fruit / sky' content and any moral negativity come from the modified head noun and the ākhira contrast, never from the root itself.

layer_attribution.occurrence_evidence: Hard spatial anchors with no world/life reading: danā 53:8, aw adnā 53:9, adnā al-arḍ 30:3, the four participles of reach (55:54, 69:23, 6:99, 76:14), and al-samāʾ al-dunyā (37:6/41:12/67:5).
layer_attribution.derivation: One skeleton in four realizations — finite verbs (danā intransitive, yudnī causative form IV), active participle (dānin/dāniyah), afʿal elative (adnā), and its feminine fuʿlā (dunyā) — a single derivational family, not four roots.
layer_attribution.lexical_class: al-dunyā is a lexicalized sub-node (frozen feminine elative 'the nearer life/abode'); the ADJ/N/T POS tallies are syntactic (attributive vs substantivized vs adverbial), cross-cutting the derivations, and are not semantic classes.
layer_attribution.contextual_relation: The scale (distance, quantity, magnitude, value, outcome) and the antonym (akthar, al-akbar, khayr, al-ākhira) are contextual; they, not the root, supply the specific dimension and any negative charge.
layer_attribution.reconciliation: 2:61 (low->inferior) and the adnā-an set (proximity-to-outcome) were preliminarily RESISTANT and reconciled to CONSISTENT via demonstrated bridges (7:169; the 33:59 verse-internal co-occurrence of yudnīna and adnā an), while being retained as adversarial boundaries.
layer_attribution.unresolved_resistance: None final-resistant. The residual honesty flag is that the low->inferior (2:61) and proximity-to-outcome (adnā an) metaphorical steps are attested but never explicitly derived by the corpus — the weakest joints of an otherwise root-wide unification.

hard_cases.reason: The only token where no physical/temporal/quantitative proximity is available; survives solely on the low->inferior extension.

evidence_basis.statement: 2:61:27:1 «أَتَسْتَبْدِلُونَ ٱلَّذِى هُوَ أَدْنَىٰ بِٱلَّذِى هُوَ خَيْرٌ»: the two exchanged items are foods, so nothing is spatially, temporally or numerically nearer; only the rank/value reading (adnā = baser/inferior, opposed to khayr) works. This is the point where the spatial-nearness nucleus is furthest from the surface, absorbed only by the low->inferior extension — which the Quran attests independently at 7:169 («عَرَضَ هَٰذَا ٱلْأَدْنَىٰ» opposed to «ٱلدَّارُ ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ») but never explicitly derives.

hard_cases.reason: «أَدْنَىٰٓ أَلَّا تَرْتَابُوٓا۟» projects proximity onto an abstract epistemic outcome; extension is inferred, not surface-derived.

evidence_basis.statement: The «أَدْنَىٰٓ أَن …» set (2:282, 4:3, 5:108, 33:51, 33:59:13:1) reads adnā as 'nearer to bringing about outcome X' = 'more conducive/apt', projecting proximity onto an abstract goal; this is consistent with the near/low-pole nucleus (proximity to a target is still proximity) but the Quran nowhere glosses the metaphor, so the proximity-to-outcome step is a reasoned extension, not a surface-demonstrated identity.

hard_case_representation.rationale: No occurrence is final-RESISTANT: the two soft edges (2:61 low->inferior, and the «adnā an …» proximity-to-outcome set) are corpus-consistent extensions of the single near/low-pole nucleus, absorbed via demonstrated bridges (7:169; 33:59 co-occurrence) rather than forced. They are recorded as ADVERSARIAL_BOUNDARY hard cases because their metaphorical step is attested but never explicitly derived by the Quran, i.e. they are the weakest joints in the unification, not counterexamples requiring a second nucleus.

rejection_condition.challenging_finding: A universal near/low-pole nucleus would be refuted if a د-ن-و occurrence required a semantic content that is NOT a near/low position on any scale — e.g. al-dunyā carrying 'world/creation' substance with no recoverable near/far framing, or an adnā/dānin token demanding affection, arrival/contact, or a fixed moral primitive independent of a contrast term.
rejection_condition.search_location: The al-dunyā mass (all 115 tokens, esp. those with no explicit ākhira antonym, e.g. 3:14:20:2, 57:20:4:2), the al-samāʾ al-dunyā triple (37:6, 41:12, 67:5), the participles (55:54, 69:23, 6:99, 76:14), and the «adnā an …» set (2:282, 4:3, 5:108, 33:51, 33:59:13:1).
rejection_condition.verification_method: For each candidate, test whether removing the near/low relation still yields the verse's sense; check whether an antonym/contrast (ākhira, khayr, akthar, al-akbar) or an elided head (ḥayāt/dār/samāʾ) supplies the extra content, versus the root itself carrying it.
rejection_condition.confounder_control: Separate root contribution from (a) the modified/elided head noun, (b) the contextual antonym that supplies negativity or the specific scale, and (c) POS artifacts (ADJ vs N vs T are syntactic, not semantic); do not let the dominant dunyā collocation be read back as the root's meaning.
rejection_condition.failure_consequence: If a token carries substance or affect the near/low relation cannot generate, the ROOT_GENERALIZATION collapses to REPRESENTATIVE/LEXICALIZED (nearness family + a frozen dunyā node) or to UNRESOLVED with an unbridged partition.

reopen_conditions: Reopen if the «أَدْنَىٰٓ أَن …» set (2:282, 4:3, 5:108, 33:51, 33:59:13:1) is shown to require a grammaticalized 'more conducive/likely' sense that cannot be reduced to proximity-to-an-outcome — this would split the elative class from the spatial nucleus.

Reopen if any al-dunyā token is found to carry 'world/creation' substance with no recoverable near/far (ākhira) framing and no elided head, breaking the bridge that 67:5 (al-samāʾ al-dunyā) and 7:169 (hādhā al-adnā) currently supply.

Reopen if 2:61 (adnā vs khayr) or 32:21 (al-ʿadhāb al-adnā vs al-akbar) is shown to encode a moral/qualitative primitive independent of any contrast term, i.e. lowness that is lexical rather than scalar.

falsification_evidence.status_rationale: A genuine refutation was run: the strongest competitor — a two-nucleus split of neutral spatial PROXIMITY (verbs, participles, adnā-of-distance, al-samāʾ al-dunyā) versus evaluative LOWNESS / a frozen al-dunyā = 'world' — was tested against the corpus and returned SUPPORTED for unity, i.e. the split failed. It is dissolved by single-word/single-verse counter-evidence: 67:5 uses al-dunyā spatially ('nearest heaven') and 7:169 puts 'this-world', 'lower-in-value', and the elative into one word (hādhā al-adnā), so a split would have to cut through single words. The claim is falsifiable (a substance-'world' or affect token would break it) and distinctive from the nearness neighbour ق-ر-ب by specifically covering the LOW/LESSER pole (quantity, magnitude, rank) and the lexicalized dunyā. The two soft edges (2:61, adnā-an) are consistent extensions, not failing occurrences requiring a second nucleus.
